result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put the recipe first on phones, cap the width on ultrawide screens and set phone padding. B sets its breakpoints where the content stops fitting (44rem + 18rem + 300px + gaps) and uses em units, so the layout also adapts when readers enlarge the text. A uses device-named tiers at fixed pixel values. B is also more concise and self-consistent, while A is longer and contradicts itself in places (160px vs 300px ad column, ingredients side by side inside a 760px cap). | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers stack the recipe first on phones, set phone padding, and cap the page on ultra-wide screens with a readable recipe width. A derives each breakpoint from the content (the recipe, rail and ad widths have to fit) and gives a tight, buildable grid-areas CSS sketch. B's breakpoints are standard device tiers with no content-based reasoning, and its CSS sketch is less complete, though its component and print guidance is useful.
